title: 2026崇禮論壇：一場未來智慧生活與下一代AI創造者的盛會
abstract: 2026崇禮論壇：一場未來智慧生活與下一代AI創造者的盛會 量子位的朋友們 2026-09-14 14:20:36 來源： 量子位 共話AI時代的生活、影像與創造。 9月12日，以“未來此刻”為主題的2026崇禮論壇在崇禮·太舞小鎮舉行。本次論壇由太舞小鎮、甲子光年、破圈文化聯合主辦，參會嘉賓、觀眾超過700人。 隨著AI逐漸進入家庭、教育、醫療、影像創作等領域，人們開始面對一組具體的問題：AI究竟會怎樣改變人的生活？我們願意把什麼交給機器，又該保留怎樣的判斷、創造與選擇？ 圍繞這些問題，本屆崇禮論壇把目光從技術本身進一步投向“智慧生活”和“創造者”。新東方創始人俞敏洪、晶泰科技聯合創始人兼首席創新官賴力鵬以及來自智慧硬體、醫療、內容創作、具身智慧和投資領域的創業者、研究者與投資人來到崇禮，從不同視角討論AI正在如何進入真實世界。甲子光年創始人&CEO張一甲在論壇現場釋出《2026AI生活方式白皮書》。 本次論壇最鮮明的特色是除了成熟創業者與產業領袖，更多年輕面孔走到了舞臺中央。 在開幕式的“小天才開麥”環節，五位來自物理AI、世界模型、算力與機器人領域的新一代創業者，圍繞《下一站，世界！》展開討論。他們談模型如何理解真實世界，也談資料、成本、應用與長期創業。論壇現場還發布了2026「AI NEXT 20」榜單，旨在關注那些仍然年輕、仍處在技術與公司快速成長階段，但已經顯露出下一代AI技術領軍者潛質的人。 下午，論壇進一步設定「智慧生活方式」「Chongli AI Film Lab」「AI Builders Show」三個專場：從AI硬體是否值得長期託付，到AI影像時代什麼仍然構成好作品，再到年輕創業者如何從Demo走向真實使用者和商業世界，討論不斷從技術能力落向真實需求。 本次崇禮論壇還啟動了首屆崇禮AI短片節，十部作品獲得“十佳未來影像獎”；而來自全國各地的AI Builders現場進行了路演，九支團隊獲評“AI Builders FUTURE 9”。 貫穿整場論壇的是一個越來越清晰的變化： AI競爭正在從“還能做什麼”，走向“為什麼值得做、誰願意長期使用、最終給人的生活帶來什麼”。 “未來此刻”因此也不只是一句關於未來的想像。它發生在一個年輕創業者剛剛形成的技術判斷裡，也發生在一件產品、一次創作，以及每一個人與AI開始建立真實關係的瞬間。 2026崇禮論壇開幕式 1. 當AI走進生活，人如何定義自己 AI能夠回答問題、生成內容、執行任務之後，人還需要培養什麼能力，又希望過怎樣的生活？開幕式的討論從這裡開始。 2026崇禮論壇開幕式現場，由擎天租提供的智元靈犀X2機器人為觀眾帶來了精彩表演 財經主持人、破圈文化創始人吳姍姍主持開幕式，來自不同領域嘉賓從各自角度出發，將技術進步與人的價值放在一起審視。 財經主持人、破圈文化創始人吳姍姍 新東方創始人俞敏洪 發表主題演講 《面對人類的豐富性，人工智慧什麼做不到》 。 他倡導在積極使用AI的同時，也認為AI存在其能力邊界，它能夠解決工具與效率的問題，卻無法替代人做最終的抉擇、也無法實現人文關懷。 在教育上，AI應當幫助孩子發現興趣、激發內驅力，讓老師有更多時間陪伴成長。 知識傳授、備課和批改可以得到AI的幫助，但一個孩子遭遇嘲笑或挫折時，仍需要老師給予情感與人格上的支援。俞敏洪強調，教師應當成為“靈魂的喚醒者”“成長的引路人”，如果技術只是讓孩子更快地做更多題，教育最重要的問題仍然沒有解決。 演講最後，他引用孟子的 “人有不為也，而後可以有為” ，提醒人們，在討論AI能為我們做什麼之前，“要先想想人工智慧不能為我們做什麼”。在使用AI之前，也要想清楚哪些事情不應該藉助它去做。 新東方創始人俞敏洪 晶泰科技聯合創始人兼首席創新官賴力鵬 在 《科技向人：AI時代的生命、健康與未來生活》 演講中，提出一個問題：當人類擁有更長的生命，該怎樣獲得更高質量的生活？在他看來，AI用於生命科學的價值，更在於幫助人類發現過去難以看到的規律，實現對每一個生命個體更精準的認知。 他介紹，晶泰將AI設計與自動化實驗連線，讓藥物設計的實驗結果繼續反饋給模型。高效的分子設計是實現有效治療的重要部分，但如何理解疾病，選擇正確的治療方向，仍取決於我們對複雜生物系統的認知深度。在晶泰科技孵化的新公司無界進化，虛擬細胞與基於RDS（遞迴科學發現）的自主科學發現的探索，正是希望讓AI參與對疾病機理的解析：提出研究假設、設計實驗方案並完成結果驗證。 在藉助AI拓展人類科研邊界的同時，他也著重強調，我們仍要保持對自然的敬畏，正視人類自身認知的侷限。 晶泰科技聯合創始人兼首席創新官賴力鵬 甲子光年創始人&CEO張一甲 釋出 《2026AI生活方式白皮書》 ，把問題進一步展開。AI正在數字、物理、科學與社會四個世界中發展，對生活的影響也從衣食住行延伸到工作方式、社會角色與自我實現。她認為，理解AI生活方式，不能僅僅停留在又有多少事情可以交給工具完成。 白皮書更本質的命題，是AI讓人獲得了更多自我定義的機會。許多過去需要專業團隊才能完成的創作，現在個人也能嘗試；一些沒有被命名的微小需求，也可以成為一個人開始做產品的理由。 “每個人都可以自我表達、自我提升、自我實現，都可以是導演、作者和遊戲設計師，都可以是世界觀的構建者。 ”張一甲說。 甲子光年創始人&CEO張一甲 三場分享聊的方向不同，但都關心同一件事： AI帶來的能力擴展，最終要回到人怎樣生活、怎樣理解自己，以及怎樣決定值得做的事。 圍繞這些問題，技術研究與人文思考需要更緊密的交流。 在先鋒問辯環節，討論的話題是 《AI走出螢幕之後，下一代入口在哪裡？》 。出門問問創始人兼CEO李志飛認為，AI時代未必會出現一個像手機那樣佔主導的硬體入口。隨著AI從被動響應變得更加主動，能夠持續理解、幫助使用者的個人助理，可能比某一種裝置更重要。 棲息地智慧住宅、恩戈羅機器人創始人沈亞楠 認同Agent的作用，但強調軟硬體一體的終端仍然重要，智慧住宅與智慧汽車這樣的空間智慧終端將在生活中扮演越來越重的角色。 唱吧創始人兼CEO陳華 則判斷，影像、影片、音樂、遊戲、程式設計等能力的突破，會分別催生新的應用機會； 商湯醫療CEO張少霆 指出，健康諮詢與嚴肅醫療需要區別看待，後者仍依賴醫院中的專業服務。 這場對話沒有將“下一代入口”歸結為一種裝置。更值得關注的變化，是人機關係從人主動操作，逐漸擴展到AI主動服務。不同產品能否成立，仍取決於它是否理解所在行業、能否為使用者提供持續的價值。 隨後，在張一甲主持的 「小天才開麥」圓桌《下一站，世界！》 中， 共績科技創始人兼CEO、深圳清華大學研究院彈性算力排程研發中心主任付智，逆矩陣科技創始人兼CRO陳博遠，明體科技創始人、北京郵電大學副教授徐夢煒，MirroS創始人兼CEO劉芳甫，以及萬格智元創始人兼CEO王冠博 ，共同討論了AI如何在真實、開放、未知的世界中學習、適應和行動。 走向物理世界是共同的方向，但突破何時到來、世界模型會如何發展，仍有分歧。劉芳甫對模型在未來一年內實現對任務與環境的動態適應持更積極判斷，並強調自進化持續學習與虛擬環境所提供的規模化訓練機會所帶來的全新可能。陳博遠更看重隱式物理規律、動作與互動，以及基模在真實場景中的反饋，並強調現在物理AI的關鍵卡點在於基模預訓練範式與真實世界資料反饋閉環。付智和徐夢煒則提醒，資料定義、表徵和訓練方法尚未充分收斂。 幾位嘉賓也把評價模型的尺度放在任務需求和使用成本上。付智判斷，推理需求會分層，分散式的小叢集有自己的機會；王冠博主張端雲協同，以更低成本滿足長期使用的需求。徐夢煒選擇太空這一任務相對明確、但工程限制嚴苛的場景，說明物理AI的應用會沿著不同需求逐步推進。陳博遠的一句話概括了這種取捨，“對於通用物理智慧的要求在於，模型能否在充滿不確定性的任意真實場景下，完成任意任務”。 對於進入家庭，嘉賓們的態度更為審慎。養老、幼兒照護等需求一直存在，但安全、隱私和技術可靠性仍影響普及；對AI自主完成任務的期待，也沒有抹去人的方向判斷。技術上的樂觀，必須與具體任務的限制放在一起討論。 談到這一代創業者的機會，付智強調從今天開始就以十年為尺度做事，陳博遠反對把物理AI歸為少數“小天才”的舞臺，重視技術積累與團隊協作。王冠博認為，這一代創業者有機會從技術出發，在具體場景中定義面向全球的通用解決方案，而解決問題本身也能帶來長期投入的動力。劉芳甫則把成功的尺度放回生活，希望AI最終幫助人“享受生活、體驗生活、分享生活”。 在上午開幕式的尾聲，崇禮論壇和「甲子光年」聯合釋出 2026「AI NEXT 20」榜單 。與尋找已經站在聚光燈下的明星創業者不同，「甲子光年」希望把視線再往前移一些，去尋找那些 仍然年輕、仍處在技術與公司快速成長階段，但已經顯露出下一代AI技術領軍者潛質的人 。 活動現場，陳博遠、付智、劉芳甫、王冠博 等人作為2026「AI NEXT 20」代表登臺，太舞小鎮總裁周文茜與張一甲為他們頒獎。 2. 智慧生活方式，怎樣才值得託付 當AI進入住宅、穿戴裝置和陪伴機器人，產品該替人做什麼，又該把哪些選擇留給人？智慧生活方式專場從這些日常問題展開。 棲息地智慧住宅、恩戈羅機器人創始人沈亞楠 發表了題為 《下一代智慧生活，從空間開始》 的演講，他提出， 下一代智慧終端將以完整空間形態為我們提供服務。 住宅首先要成為軟硬體一體的產品，通過中央算力、融合感知和統一控制，讓家成為一個整體協同工作，AI才能從執行指令走向主動服務。例如， 只有完整的智慧住宅中， 才能實現體驗上升與能耗下降的超級“五恆”體驗。下一步在智慧住宅中， 具身機器人將依託“車路協同” 而率先實現收納、清潔等物理服務。 棲息地智慧住宅、恩戈羅機器人創始人沈亞楠 明勢創投合夥人焦騰 從“被託付的日常”切入。他的演講 《被託付的日常：AI硬體“接管”生活與人性留白》 給出一個判斷：AI硬體正從工具走向代理，進而承擔使用者託付的日常事務，而託付背後代表了更深的信任。真正有機會的產品，需要高頻使用、持續積累對使用者和場景的理解，並通過服務反饋改進判斷。同時託付也意味著生活的一部分被授權給機器，因此授權應當可見、可逆、可撤回，決策過程需要能夠解釋。高價值判斷仍應由人完成，遺忘、猶豫和不被記錄的時刻，也應當被保留下來。把人從繁瑣的工作解放出來，把意義留給自己。 明勢創投合夥人焦騰 在 誠美資本董事總經理王迪 主持的 《AI硬體的下一站：是真需求，還是新一輪智慧裝置幻覺？》 圓桌中，嘉賓們討論了一個共同的問題：AI硬體怎樣讓使用者少費力，同時提供值得持續使用的價值？ CyboPal創始人彭天放 選擇從功能價值切入，讓人在電腦前通過對話交代任務、監督執行； 雪夢未來創始人秦旭 則認為，新的計算平臺需要新的互動方式，眼鏡與神經腕帶的結合有望帶來低摩擦，無感式，隱式式的互動。 光智時空COO郜新陸 看重無感記錄，讓那些沒有被主動拍攝、卻值得日後回看的生活片段得以留下。 蝸牛睡眠聯合創始人竹東翔 希望通過連續佩戴，理解使用者一整天的身體規律，而非僅記錄入睡和醒來的時間。 情感產品面對的考驗有所不同。 酷奇奇聯合創始人蔣軍 強調，依託於角色引擎的角色可持續生長、與使用者高質量互動，才助於把使用者長期留下。 達晨財智業務合夥人王晗 則把“主動託付”作為判斷標準：使用者是否願意把身體資料、重要對話和睡眠環境交給產品？王晗認為，信任、審美和對人真實情緒的理解，會影響AI硬體能否長久留在人們的生活裡。 接下來， 兵器工業集團遠山智行副總經理任敬偉 發表了演講 《遠山智行：人機協同的下一個時代》 ，他指出，外骨骼走進日常生活的關鍵，是從感知人的動作進一步走向預測人的意圖。人在行走中想停下來看看風景，裝置如果還繼續邁步，就會造成不適。材料、能源和控制演算法的進步，加上AI對運動意圖的識別，讓人機協同有了改善。他希望外骨骼能夠像衣服一樣輕鬆穿戴，從功能層面不僅是一個單獨助行器，而是作為集助力助行、身體狀態評估、運動風險提示的智慧穿戴平臺。 兵器工業集團遠山智行副總經理任敬偉 在 《用3D對抗時間：智慧時代的情感存檔與生活方式重塑》 演講中， Remy聯合創始人王正男 提出，用3D記錄三維世界，可以儲存照片和影片難以完整留下的空間體驗。Remy將手機拍攝的影片重建為可互動的3D空間，讓即將搬離的家、曾經生活過的宿舍有機會被保留下來。考慮到現有社交平臺主要傳播二維內容，團隊又把3D模型轉成特效影片，方便使用者分享。 Remy聯合創始人王正男 隨後，在題為 《AI是新朋友，還是新裝備？》 的圓桌討論中，幾位嘉賓都表示希望陪伴產品補足現實生活中的情感需求，同時保留人與人的關係；對於AI能否成為朋友，他們的判斷有所不同。 超級玩伴聯合創始人陳嘉陽 認為，依賴不等於成功。對超級玩伴而言，未來五年，多數使用者仍會把AI視為認知能力的延伸；AI要成為真正的朋友，還有很長的路。 Robonova創始人吳恆 則更看好親情、愛情、友情之外的“第四種關係”，讓人可以表達脆弱、獲得回應，減少人際交往中的顧慮。 無論科技聯合創始人梁聰 強調，機器人的生命感來自自然的情感表達，無須追求完全復刻真人；表達情感也可以成為已有產品的一項新能力。 貝陪科技創始人黃纓寧 把建立關係的前提說得更具體：“AI如果想成為人類寄託感情的朋友，必須先得是一個提供價值的裝備。”產品先在明確的場景中幫到使用者，陪伴和信任才有機會在長期相處中形成。 3. AI影像，抵達創作目的地 「Chongli AI Film Lab」專場啟動了 首屆崇禮AI短片節 。 太舞小鎮、甲子光年、破圈文化、生數科技與Artidence聯合發起活動 ，邀請創作者圍繞“記憶與創想”“未來此刻”兩個命題展開創作。比起AI影像創作工具本身，這個專場更關心的是如何讓創作者個人的審美和經驗留下來，打造出真正的好故事。 與光同塵聯合創始人鄭瀏博 發表 《AI影像時代：精品影像創制》 演講。他認為，AI縮短了想像變成畫面的過程，但好的作品依然需要創意判斷和團隊協作。創作者要發揮已有專長，找到能夠養活自己的業務，才有機會繼續拍電影。他也建議讓真人實拍保留情感可信度，用AI補充現實拍攝難以實現的想像。 與光同塵聯合創始人鄭瀏博 接下來的圓桌 《目的地如何被重新拍出來？》 ，由 清華大學蘇世民學者兼Artidence創始人趙康登主持 。在這裡，“目的地”既是旅行地點，也是作品要抵達的觀眾。多個AI影像創作者共同討論，當AI讓畫面更容易生成以後，故事怎樣打動人，又怎樣被人看見。 虎山行AI創意工作室創始人、導演孔德飛 看重個人經驗與情感，主張作品接受普通觀眾的檢驗，無需因AI製作而獲得額外寬容。 OiiOii合夥人兼國內業務負責人周爽 期待工具幫助更多人表達，同時拓寬想像。 星雲CEO兼靈矩科技聯合創始人呂少龍 更關心分發，以及內容能否為目的地帶來增長。 Tapas Entertainment中國總經理李瀟 則提醒，精品要符合各自品類的製作與商業標準，出海還要理解當地文化。孔德飛從夢境、音樂現場等個人感受出發，李瀟則重視經過市場驗證的IP。兩種創作起點在討論中並存。幾位嘉賓都把故事放在重要位置，但並未用同一把尺子衡量精品。 接下來，短片節入圍的十部作品在現場展映。經過評委現場打分評選， 《出廠設定》《太舞少年》《FOMO》分別獲得首屆崇禮AI短片節“未來影像TOP 3”冠軍、亞軍、季軍。 冠軍彭思瑞 的 《出廠設定》 設想了一個由 AI 構建完美幻象的未來世界，並由此追問真實與擬像之間的邊界； 亞軍花花 的 《太舞少年》 講述一名滑雪少年不斷突破自我、向陽成長的故事，將少年的蛻變與太舞小鎮十二年的山野發展同頻交織； 季軍吳德堪 在作品 《FOMO》 中討論了一個更深刻的命題，AI技術的日新月異加深了每個人的焦慮，但任何事情都並得一蹴而就，允許自己慢慢沉澱、打磨，或許才能真正成功。 另外的7部影片也都獲得了“十佳未來影像獎”。創作者 陳茂源 的 《太舞來客》 關注人與人的連線； 劉作宇 的 《夜神道》 講述未來救援中的衝突； 曲奕昕 的 《機器人借走的夏天》 藉機器人一場有限期的陪伴，叩問陪伴是否真的能被替代； 陳豔 的 《崇禮的風會治癒每一個女孩》 以一段有溫度的友情為線索，講述女性在陪伴與治癒中重新生長、找回自我的成長曆程； 李宜霏 的 《為尚未歸來的人》 藉機器人的探索儲存人類的牽掛； 張豔婷 的 《人生曠野》 講主動停下來，關注普通又平凡的日常生活； 於家祥 的 《花·瓶》 以童話表達親情、公益與環保。 專場現場還進行了《評委面對面：好作品的標準變了嗎？》 為主題的圓桌討論。四位嘉賓同時也是首屆崇禮AI短片節評委的共同回答是，情感、敘事和作者表達仍是核心，技術表現在評選中所佔的比重則在變化。 中國傳媒大學動畫與數字藝術學院影視藝術學院碩導、北京國際電影節AIGC單元負責人唐俊淑 認為，本屆入圍作品的技術瑕疵已不再妨礙敘事； 北京電影學院數字媒體學院副教授、中國工藝美術學會新媒體藝術專業委員會副秘書長吳限 提醒，達到專業完成度仍有難關。 中國傳媒大學教授、動畫製片人艾勝英 更關心可信的角色和經得起時間檢驗的故事，認為作品要先讓觀眾形成預期，再給出意料之外的展開。 AI藝術家、跨界製作人、中國傳媒大學專業碩導陳劉芳 則區分個人創作、商業作品與參賽作品，提醒創作者別因迎合評價而偏離初衷。 4. AI Builders Show，青年創業者的嘗試與堅持 把想法做成初步產品更容易，找到願意長期使用的人，依然需要反覆嘗試。「AI Builders Show」專場圍繞青年們的創業過程和他們的產品展開。 張一甲 在 《甲子Builders——共識之前》 演講中，向大家介紹了「甲子Builders」品牌。她希望把對早期創業者的發現與陪伴長期做下去，讓正在做產品的人有機會認識同行、交流經驗，也找到能提供實際幫助的人。 荊華密算創始人兼CEO林修醇 發表 《AI的競賽，正在從“好不好用”轉向“敢不敢用”》 演講，主張把資料安全納入AI採用的前提，並介紹基於高效能密態計算保護AI資料的解決方案，推動密態計算從技術能力向AI時代的基礎設施演進。 荊華密算創始人兼CEO林修醇 共生知行創始人兼CEO丁鵬翔 在 《AI Builders正在改變什麼？》 演講中，倡導選擇值得解決的問題、把團隊長板做到極致，並持續提高實驗迭代速度。他播放了人形機器人開卡丁車的演示影片，介紹團隊如何把想法用於實際任務。 共生知行創始人兼CEO丁鵬翔 演講環節結束後，專場進入Demo Battle環節，九支創業團隊依次登臺，他們的Demo按清晨、白天與夜晚分為三組，每隊用8分鐘展示、4分鐘接受問答。 清晨組， 覺醒意志Awak創始人兼CEO李恭略 介紹以智慧穿戴裝置記錄睡眠與健康的產品； 小球圈創始人楊光垚 介紹基於端雲混合模型的AI運動陪伴產品，提供運動影片剪輯，技術指導等功能。 flowTU CTO趙經博 關注音樂的精細修改，讓使用者縮短副歌、替換樂器，同時保留滿意的部分。

title: AI開始改進“改進自己的方法”，RSI進入平方時代丨MetaRSI
abstract: AI開始改進“改進自己的方法”，RSI進入平方時代丨MetaRSI 思邈 2026-09-14 11:45:46 來源： 量子位 小模型突破瓶頸，旗艦模型開啟新空間 允中 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 讓模型自己生成訓練資料、自己改寫提示詞、自己修復程式碼，這條路線被稱為： 遞迴自我改進（Recursive Self-Improvement，RSI） 。 但幾乎所有RSI系統都是同一套結構：一個固定不變的改程序序，反覆作用於模型。並往往只從Harness、Data或Model RSI的單一視角切入。 為了回應這一難題，CosmosMind聯合斯坦福、伯克利、MIT、清華、北大等十餘家海內外高校釋出MetaRSI-v1。 這是 全球首個統一Model-RSI、Data-RSI、Harness-RSI的元遞迴架構 ，能夠改進“自我改進的過程”。 RSI由此進入“平方時代”。 △論文首頁 在沒有任何外部教師模型參與下 ，MetaRSI-v1使得一個僅30億啟用參數的小模型， 在四項基準上平均自我提升10.9分 ；並且讓GPT-5.6、Claude Opus 5等六款前沿旗艦模型， 平均提升7.3分 。 更重要的是數字背後， MetaRSI-v1是一套試圖 統一整個RSI領域的架構語言 ：包括一個核心、兩條編排軸、三個運算元、整個元RSI層，以及五大定律。 △MetaRSI-v1概覽 首次被統一的Loop Kernel範式 Loop Kernel是MetaRSI-v1首次提出的自我改進統一形式。 它第一次把“進步如何發生”抽象成一條與物件無關的閉環：消費反饋得到的學習訊號，在Data、Harness、Model上提出改動，交由驗證器裁決，並將結果迴流為下一輪訊號。 Data、Harness、Model從此開始能夠被統一成同一Kernel的不同例項化運算元 ，可組合、可統一排程，自我改進由此第一次擁有了統一、可複用的底層骨架。 △Loop Kernel範式 改進空間：Data-RSI、Harness-RSI、Model-RSI 沿用同一個Loop Kernel，自我改進在三個空間上展開，分別由Data-RSI、Harness-RSI、Model-RSI三個運算元承擔並協同完成。 Data-RSI ：從自身執行軌跡提取學習訊號，經校驗用於合成數據交由下游消費，標定並放大模型正向能力與負向能力邊界。 Harness-RSI ：利用學習反饋訊號，在Harness拆分出的System Prompt、Skill、MCP、Tools、Memory五個可插拔槽位上生成改進，做加法與減法。 Model-RSI ：更新模型自身的參數與結構，把反覆驗證有效的行為內化進模型。 縱橫之間：讓改進自己找到最優路徑 橫軸（horizontal orchestration）編排運算元的應用順序 ：RSI² Agent在每個決策點根據訊號反饋選定下一個運算元，再把該運算元有機銜接編排送入RSI Loop Kernel執行。 縱軸（vertical optimization）最佳化運算元的內部策略 ：RSI² Agent向目標運算元專屬的RSI² Sub-Agent下發指令，後者根據學習訊號與環境反饋等改寫運算元本身的RSI規則，最佳化RSI系統本身。 遞迴之上的遞迴：三層改進與“元層”的誕生 整套架構由四個Agent協調運作，並且均能被人類專家局部替換形成human-in-the-loop系統。 MetaRSI² Agent ：學習如何進行合適的縱橫最佳化，最佳化 RSI² Agent 的策略學習。 RSI² Agent ：在每個決策點選擇進行橫軸（指定下一個運算元）或縱軸（向Sub-Agent下發策略改寫指令）最佳化。 RSI² Sub-Agent ：在縱向最佳化中，接受來自 RSI² Agent的 執行指令，對運算元內部的RSI策略進行調整。 Transition Agent：負責銜接橫向編排中上游運算元的產物與下一個運算元對產物的消費。 四個Agent對應形成三個RSI最佳化Level：運算元改進目標系統，雙軸編排改進運算元用法，元層改進雙軸編排策略本身。 實驗：小模型與前沿模型均實現自我進化 實驗沿兩條路線展開： 小模型路線 使用可訓練的開源模型，Data、Harness、Model三個運算元全部啟用； 前沿模型路線 面向Claude Opus 5，GPT-5.6 sol，Kimi K3等頂級模型，這類模型參數巨大或為閉源模型，僅啟用Data與Harness運算元。 路線一：小模型的自我改進 目標模型為Qwen3.5-35B-A3B（35B總參、3B啟用），在Terminal-Bench 2.1、SWE-bench Pro、GPQA-Diamond高難度子集、AIME四項基準上評測。 △MetaRSI讓Qwen3.5-35B-A3B實現自進化 MetaRSI-v1平均提升10.9分，SWE-bench Pro 解決率接近翻倍 ，Meta層為RSI帶來更高的天花板， 連續自進化的累計增益提升顯著 。 △“改進改進者”，MetaRSI讓小模型累計自進化增益擴大 路線二：前沿模型的自我改進 多款前沿模型在Terminal-Bench 2.1上平均提升7.3分，說明MetaRSI範式對前沿模型同樣成立， 旗艦模型同樣留有可觀的自我改進空間 。 △六款前沿模型的自我改進 五條定律：為“機器如何進步”立法 MetaRSI梳理出 兩條互補的改進路線 ：Harness-RSI保持權重不變，讓自我改進覆蓋任何可通過介面呼叫的模型；Model-RSI通過訓練把能力內化進模型。 且MetaRSI首次重新定義了Data-RSI，作為模型的能力邊界探測與放大器，通過對執行軌跡與外界反饋learning-signal的聯合分析得到經過驗證的經驗並scale為可複用的資料，並標定這些經驗能夠支撐到哪裡，框定模型能力的正、負邊界。 Data-RSI的產物同時供給Harness-RSI與Model-RSI消費，兩條路線的改動結果又能夠流回Data-RSI，重新標定能力邊界、驅動下一輪，能力由此逐輪披露、累積。 在這一過程中，Harness不僅能做加法還能做減法：Data-RSI放大暴露的問題經Model-RSI內化之後，原本吸納在Harness中的知識會變成冗餘，Harness-RSI系統在回放校驗下將其刪除，能力留下，成本退場。 在此之上，MetaRSI提煉出五條定律。 定律一：驗證決定自我改進的前沿。 一個領域能不能形成自改進閉環，取決於該領域任務能否被檢驗，是否有合適的verifier。 定律二：自我認知會過期，重新發現能力邊界是速率瓶頸，RSI改變agent能力，其原本舊的系統描述隨即失效。 定律三：能力與載體無關但成本與載體有關。 例如同一項能力放在Harness裡每次推理都要重付成本，內化進Model只需付一次，成熟迴圈能夠持續把能力遷移到更便宜的載體。 定律四：可信度由不可寫面度量。 在閉環內部，真正能力變強和放寬成功標準會得到完全相同的分數，而且這種偏差從內部無法察覺、也無法靠統計糾正。 定律五：迴圈不憑空創造能力，一切增益本質上都是外部資訊熵的輸入或能力的激發。 自改進只能重新組織、放大並固化模型已經具備的潛力。因此每次提升都要分清兩部分：哪些是把已有能力放大出來的，哪些是真正從外部新引入的。 環環相扣，終成文明：讓每個科學領域都擁有進化閉環 人類歷史每一次的躍遷，都源於“生產答案的方式被重新發明”。 MetaRSI要在AI時代把這件事再做一遍。 它背後的CosmosMind團隊，是一支由 清華/北大/斯坦福等海內外名校碩博、頭部大廠基模核心組研究員、著名產業方領軍人物 組成的小而精的團隊，長期從事大規模模型訓練/RSI/智慧體/科學計算等工作，在頂會頂刊上發表過諸多有影響力的論文。 這一次，他們沒有選擇再做一個更大的模型，而是把全部精力押在了“ 改進改進本身 ”這件事上。 團隊同步了開源RSI-Harness，這是一個能自我學習、自我迭代的Harness，並可以在使用中為不同科學領域與工程實踐沉澱出可移植的 Harness Genome 。 Cosmosmind已經把目光投向了閉環觸碰物理世界：可程式設計儀器、自動化實驗室成為執行器和驗證器，模擬、臺架實驗、真實儀器可以像三級火箭一樣逐級推進，把不可逆的昂貴操作放到最後——第一個在物理世界關上的進化迴圈，很可能不會出現在開放環境裡，而會出現在 自動化實驗室 中。 研究者面對的不再是一堆待驗證的猜測。人類只需負責定義問題與價值判斷，而機器負責讓“從假設到驗證”的迴圈，以過去無法想像的速度開始轉動。 相信在MetaRSI的後時代，AI將會從解題工具走向文明級的進化引擎。 Cosmomind官網：https://cosmosmind.ai/ 專案主頁：https://github.com/CosmosMind-ai/RSI-Harness title: 中國物理AI大突破：PhysBrain 1.5登頂全球開源榜一，空間智慧與GPT-6 Astra並駕齊驅
abstract: 中國物理AI大突破：PhysBrain 1.5登頂全球開源榜一，空間智慧與GPT-6 Astra並駕齊驅 允中 2026-09-14 11:18:42 來源： 量子位 這家中國公司，剛跑完了物理閉環裡最難的一段路 允中 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 物理AI，正在成為2026年全球人工智慧最關鍵的賽道，也是未來之爭。 大模型用了三年時間把“ 會說話、會思考、會工作 ”推到極致，但當行業開始追問“模型能不能走進真實世界、能不能動手”時，一扇新的大門被推開。 Google DeepMind於2026年7月30日釋出Gemini Robotics 2，基於Gemini 3.5 Flash的“具身推理”大腦ER 2，試圖讓機器人“邊看影片邊想下一步”。近期，OpenAI GPT-6引發行業熱議，推理、程式設計與多模態理解能力再度突破，把通用智慧的天花板又推高了一截。 而Robocurve的一次實驗，又將“大語言模型是否能在真實世界中行動”這個問題擺在了臺前。該實驗將GPT-6 Astra部署在真實機械臂上，在20次“積木放入碗”任務裡，GPT-6 Astra完成19次，而Claude Fable 5.1僅完成8次。 這次實驗表明，基座模型能力大幅提升之後，也可以在具身任務上取得可觀的表現。 但頂尖大語言模型在具身操作上仍有鴻溝。Robocurve同一套測試的另一面很說明問題：在“藍色拼圖塊對位插入凹槽”這種毫米級精細任務上，GPT-6 Astra的成功率從95%掉到10%。 大模型積累的通用理解，可以跨越“看懂”到“粗動作”的鴻溝，卻仍在“精細接觸、精準插入”面前止步。 這正是全行業共同的瓶頸，也是後來者真正的機會視窗。 就在這個關口，一家從北京海淀中關村走出來的中國公司—— 深度機智 ，交出了自己的答卷。 2026年9月9日，深度機智正式釋出物理基座模型PhysBrain 1.5，在28項公開基準上取得72.5的綜合均分，位居參評開源模型首位，與頭部閉源模型GPT-6 Astra（73.3）、Gemini 3.6 Flash（73.0）的差距，已收窄到1分以內。 它沒有去和巨頭比拼參數規模，也沒有去追逐各類技術熱點，而是用一條“人類學習”的技術路線，把物理智慧基礎模型能力作為核心戰略方向持續深耕。 GPT-6 Astra的機械臂實驗恰恰印證了，把基礎模型做紮實，才是決定物理智慧上限的關鍵變數，這正是深度機智長期踐行的方向。 PhysBrain 1.5是深度機智在這一戰略方向上持續投入的階段性成果。 在28項基準測評中，PhysBrain 1.5取得 14項 開源第一，10項位列開源第二。 它不是在某一個單項上刷出了高分，而是在空間理解、動作生成、未來狀態預測的完整能力鏈條上，全線躋身開源模型前列。 這意味著PhysBrain 1.5提供的不只是“更聰明的感知”，而是機器人從理解環境到執行任務的系統性基礎能力。 PhysBrain 1.5全面開源，技術報告、2B與8B模型權重、評測工具包，全部向社群開放，讓更多全球開發者基於同一套基座，共同探索物理智慧的下一步。 Project Page: https://deepcybo-physai.github.io/PhysBrain-1.5 Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/collections/DeepCybo/physbrain-15 Evaluation Kit: https://github.com/DeepCybo-PhysAI/PhysBrainEvalKit 開源第一，比肩頂尖閉源：中國物理AI基座模型站上全球前沿 物理基座模型的評測向來是件難事。評估PhysBrain 1.5的，是一組28項公開基準，按五大能力維度組織——視覺空間感知、空間與多視角理解、具身認知與規劃、空間指向與可供性、視覺軌跡推理。 在這套多維測試中，PhysBrain 1.5-8B拿下72.5的綜合均分，排開源陣營第一。 從結果上看，PhysBrain 1.5-8B以72.5的綜合均分拿下開源模型榜首，並在28項中的14項取得開源最佳，10項位列開源模型第二；相較當前最強開源對手Hy-Embodied-VLM-1.0（66.0）高出約6.5分，較RynnBrain 1.1（63.1）高出9.4分。 更受關注的是其整體水位：72.5分這一成績，與GPT-6 Astra（73.3）、Gemini 3.6 Flash（73.0）的差距已收窄到1分以內。在具身智慧的核心能力上，深度機智已經與全球最前沿的閉源模型站在同一水位線上。 分項成績同樣能說明問題。 在RoboSpatial-Home空間理解取得73.9分，意味著模型能夠在真實場景中準確理解物體之間的空間關係，這是機器人在真實環境中操作的前提。 Part-Affordance可操作部位識別拿下84.0分，說明模型不僅能理解“物體是什麼”，更理解“這個物體的哪個部位可以被操作、應該怎麼操作”，這是從“識別”走向“互動”的關鍵一步。 RoboRefit視覺目標定位獲得89.8分，則表示模型能夠在複雜場景中精準找到並鎖定目標物體，為後續動作執行提供了可靠的視覺錨點。 這些成績說明了PhysBrain 1.5的領先並非局部優勢，而是一種覆蓋感知、空間、推理、規劃與定位的系統性能力領先。這也標誌著具身基座模型的競爭，正在從單項能力的較量，進入系統能力的對決。 比8B榜首成績更值得注意的，是PhysBrain 1.5並沒有只做一個“大版本”。 深度機智同步開放了PhysBrain 1.5-2B與PhysBrain 1.5-8B兩檔參數規模。在專案頁最新公佈的同一套28項測試中，PhysBrain 1.5-2B取得66.6分。 按照官方評測規則，2B版本僅作為參考，不參與開源排名；但如果只比較數值，它的綜合得分已經超過表中所有其他非PhysBrain開源參評模型，包括30A3B規模的Hy-Embodied-VLM-1.0（66.0）、8B的Embodied-R1.5（64.9）和9B的RynnBrain 1.1（63.1）。 這讓2B版本呈現出另一種價值：它不是8B模型的“展示性縮小版”，而是在顯著降低參數規模之後，仍然保留了相當完整的具身理解能力。 對於開發者而言，這意味著更低的試用、部署和二次開發門檻；對於PhysBrain而言，則意味著同一技術路線開始同時覆蓋“效能上限”和“輕量可用”兩個方向。 △ HF社群使用者線上進行模型demo測試， demo網址：https://huggingface.co/spaces/hugging-apps/physbrain1-5-8b-demo 兩個版本現均已上線Hugging Face，為社群驗證與下游部署提供入口（https://huggingface.co/collections/DeepCybo/physbrain-15）。 在上線僅3天時間內，PhysBrian 1.5就獲得了超過3k的下載量，為全球開發者社群提供了媲美頂尖閉源模型的物理智慧基座能力。 從人類經驗到物理智慧迴圈：Ego360與Physical Loop的理念閉環 72.5分是一個數字成績，但在數字之外更值得討論的，是PhysBrain 1.5選擇的“路徑”——被深度機智稱為“Physical Loop”物理智慧迴圈的統一架構。 深度機智把物理智慧的本質歸納為一個迴圈：觀察世界、理解空間與任務、判斷動作後果、執行、再依據新的觀察修正下一步，即Physical Loop。 真正的物理智慧，不是單點能力的堆砌，而是這個閉環能夠連續、穩定地運轉，並根據反饋自我修正。 因此PhysBrain 1.5將“觀察世界—理解空間與任務—判斷動作後果—執行—反饋修正”這五步原本分散在不同模型裡的能力，重新組織進了同一個基座模型。 過去，物理AI系統普遍是“理解模型+動作模型+預測模型”拼接，拼接意味著每個子模型都要單獨訓練、單獨調優。 深度機智的判斷是：要做出能“在世界中行動並自我修正”的底座，必須先回到這個閉環本身，把能力重新組織起來。PhysBrain 1.5，正是圍繞這一閉環重建模型本身。 模型如何學會這個迴圈？ 如果訓練資料只告訴模型“世界長什麼樣”，卻沒有保留下“人在什麼情境下采取什麼動作，以及動作之後世界發生了什麼變化”，那麼再統一的模型，也很難真正學到物理互動的規律。 這正是深度機智把“人類經驗”放在資料起點上的原因。 深度機智認為，人類經驗天然地嵌入這一迴圈：個體在真實世界裡不斷感知情境、產生意圖、採取行動，並根據結果調整後續行為；人類的智慧，正是在這種反覆互動與修正中逐步生長出來的。 團隊在論文中寫得很直白：“物理感知的預訓練監督，完全來自人類互動影片”。在深度機智的技術路線裡，人類經驗是物理智慧迴圈的第一性來源。 支撐這一技術判斷的，是深度機智構建的 Ego360人類全景真實資料體系 。 它通過全景影片記錄任務執行時的周圍環境，並同步保留全身姿態、手部運動與任務級語音，使一段互動不再只是孤立的“動作片段”，同時還具有更連續的任務、動作與狀態變化上下文。 這種連續性很重要。模型不需要學習“手應該往哪裡動”，還需要知道當前處於什麼情境、為什麼要執行這一步，以及任務推進後環境如何變化。 這也是人類互動影片相對於碎片化操作資料更核心的價值。 前不久在WAIC 2026（2026世界人工智慧大會暨人工智慧全球治理高級別會議）的具身智慧空間互動論壇上，深度機智創始人 陳凱博士 就以《人類學習範式：物理通用智慧遠征的起點》為題，公開系統闡述了以人類真實互動經驗支撐物理通用智慧的技術判斷，並展示了圍繞全景人類資料展開的實踐進展。 9月10日， 國家 資料局 黨組書記、局長劉烈宏主持召開具身智慧座談會。深度機智受邀出席 ，並展示了人類全景真實資料與情境數採（In Context Data Collection）範式。 能夠參與這場閉門座談，既是對深度機智資料路徑的認可，也意味著一家企業的技術選擇，上升為行業基礎設施層面的參考座標。 從2025年12月提出情境數採範式，到2026年7月全景數採範式的迭代，深度機智在半年多時間裡完成了資料採集能力的迭代，並同步推進大規模人類真實資料採集與模型驅動的全自動標註管線。 PhysBrain 1.5進一步將人類互動影片真正納入Physical Loop的預訓練框架，這條路線開始從判斷和理念，變為大規模資料運營和模型能力。 △ 2026年7月，深度機智創始人陳凱在WAIC論壇釋出全景數採方案 理解、動作、預測：一個基座裡的三大能力 如果說Physical Loop回答的是“物理智慧應該如何運轉”，那麼PhysBrain 1.5接下來解決的，就是“這些能力如何在一個模型裡被共同學習”。 具體來說，它基於開源基礎模型，將語言回答、空間座標、動作軌跡、未來畫面與深度預測，全部納入同一套訓練框架，不需要為每種能力單獨搭建模組或設計專門的輸出層，讓模型在“看懂世界”“生成動作”和“預判結果”之間形成內在一致性，而非鬆散拼接。 由此，具身理解、動作生成與未來狀態預測，不再是三個彼此獨立的模型，而能夠在Physical Loop中彼此約束、協同演進。 一是具身理解：知道“此刻發生了什麼” PhysBrain 1.5保留了VLM影像與影片理解的介面，通過具身監督為其注入物理感知能力。訓練資料覆蓋基礎視覺空間感知、3D與多視角空間理解、具身認知推理與規劃、空間指向與可供性，以及視覺軌跡推理，五大能力。 這意味著模型不僅“看到”畫面，還帶著空間結構、物理常識和任務意圖去理解場景。它輸出的不只是語言描述，還包括結構化的空間座標與軌跡目標，這些正是後續動作生成所需的關鍵錨點。 二是動作生成，指向的是“接下來該怎麼做” PhysBrain 1.5模型通過Human-as-Humanoid管線，從人類影片中學習手腕的運動方式，將其轉化為機器人可以執行的動作。給定當前畫面、任務指令和之前的動作歷史，模型能夠直接生成接下來一系列的動作步驟。 更重要的是，這套動作能力不綁定特定機器人，同一份模型可以適配不同形態、不同控制頻率的機器人，無需為每臺機器單獨訓練。 三是未來狀態預測：預見“做完之後會發生什麼” PhysBrain 1.5在給定當前畫面與任務指令後，可以預測1秒後的物理狀態，並同時輸出三種模態：RGB影像、深度圖和機器人掩碼。 這三者空間對齊、彼此關聯，共同描述一個完整的未來場景。這種“先想像結果、再採取行動”的能力，讓模型在閉環中擁有了前瞻與糾錯的依據，動作尚未執行，它已能預判環境將如何變化。 三項能力被納入同一個模型、同一套訓練框架，不再各自獨立。理解提供場景證據，動作生成延續物理互動，未來預測給出前瞻訊號，三者互為輸入、互相約束，共同支撐Physical Loop的連續運轉。 這也標誌著物理智慧的構建方式，正在從“拼裝專用模組”走向“訓練統一基座”。 Human-as-Humanoid：人類動作進入模型，再走向機器人 PhysBrain 1.5還有一個很容易被忽略的關鍵問題：人類影片中的動作，究竟如何變成模型能夠學習、機器人能夠使用的動作表示？ 這裡連線人類資料與動作模型的，正是深度機智此前提出的Human-as-Humanoid框架。 在PhysBrain 1.5的訓練過程中，團隊通過Human-as-Humanoid的轉換框架，實現人類行為資料從“可觀看的記錄”到“可訓練的資源”的轉化，讓人類行為資料成為動作建模可持續、可規模化的燃料來源。 這正是human-centric data進入action modeling的關鍵橋樑。 而在此前的Human-as-Humanoid研究中，這條轉換鏈路已經進一步延伸到自研的60自由度擬人體機器人Prime U上，對“人的動作經驗能否遷移到機器人”進行了真機驗證。 在研究中，其原始示範吞吐量達到傳統遙操作的4.8至7.2倍，並在部分任務上實現了從人類資料到真機執行的零樣本遷移，模型不必看到特定機器人本體的示範，就能在該本體上執行相應任務。 從這裡再回看深度機智的全棧佈局，它的邏輯就變得清晰：Ego360持續積累人類經驗，PhysBrain基座模型以這些資料不斷拓展能力邊界，Human-as-Humanoid承擔人類動作與機器人動作空間之間的轉換，Prime系列本體則在真實互動中提供驗證與反饋。 資料、大腦與本體，被組織在同一條主線上持續演進。這意味著深度機智已經獨立完成了“從模型能力到本體驗證”的完整閉環。 這種全棧能力，不僅意味著更快的迭代速度和更低的協同成本，更意味著一種系統性的壁壘。 提前一年的路線定力：當全球共識追上深度機智的判斷 回看這場競賽，多數參與者默認了一個隱含前提：物理智慧是“大模型順手能做好的延伸”，先把語言能力推到極致，再給模型接上動作輸出，問題便解決了。 GPT-6 Astra的機械臂實驗讓我們看到了通用基礎模型的提升，可以轉化為物理行動能力，但其在精細操作上的侷限同樣說明，僅靠語言模型的通用能力並不足夠，物理智慧需要專門的基礎模型。 這側面印證了深度機智一直以來的戰略判斷：物理基座模型不是短期風口，而是一項需要長期投入的佈局，先想清楚“物理智慧究竟該從哪裡長出來”，再讓資料、模型與本體圍繞這一長期目標持續組織、協同推進。 把時間線往回撥一年。2025年10月10日，深度機智就釋出了《源於人，超越人》技術路線圖，明確把“人類學習”作為物理通用智慧的核心研發路徑，並圍繞“以人類資料為起點、以動作為中心建模、身體為AI設計”三大戰略，開展資料、模型、本體全棧佈局。 在深度機智的邏輯裡，物理智慧不可能靠把網際網路文本“翻譯”成動作獲得。人是在真實世界裡，通過一遍遍“看見—嘗試—被反饋修正”長出操作能力的，人類是物理智慧最好的老師。 當時，行業對“用人類第一視角資料訓基座模型”遠未形成共識；而2026年PI、NVIDIA、Dyna乃至學術界的集體轉向，恰恰在一年後驗證了深度機智一年前的判斷“人類經驗是物理智慧的第一性來源”。深度機智不是這一趨勢的追隨者，而是它的先發者。 這種先發，不只是判斷上的領先，更是工程上的積累。回看PhysBrain的迭代節奏，2026年3月27日PhysBrain 1.0在中關村論壇釋出，2026年9月9日PhysBrain 1.5跟進，半年一次的高頻迭代，意味著這家公司正一步步把路線圖走實，建立起穩定的研發閉環與工程能力。 Google DeepMind的Gemini Robotics、Physical Intelligence的π系列、Figure AI、NVIDIA Cosmos 3……全球頭部機構正沿不同路徑加速佈局，物理智慧的研發投入顯著提速。 深度機智在人類學習路線上的早期佈局所形成的先發積累，與資料、模型、本體全棧協同的系統能力相結合，正在成為全球物理智慧競爭中一項難以複製的關鍵優勢。 扛起行業發展重任的“黑馬” 全球開源第一，只是PhysBrain 1.5在這一時間點上交出的成績單。背後更值得關注的，是它在物理AI這一仍處早期的賽道上展示出來的三種能力： 一是架構的統一性。 深度機智把“理解、動作、預測”收進同一個自迴歸主幹，讓物理智慧迴圈真正在模型內部閉環，而不是靠多個子模型拼接； 二是資料路線的差異化。 深度機智率先以大模型方法論，把人類第一視角資料作為物理常識來源，在行業裡推進了稀缺的資料基建； 三是工程落地的全棧性。 深度機智從Ego360數採、PhysBrain基座、Prime系列本體到Human-as-Humanoid轉換框架，每一環都自己把控。 物理智慧的終局，不是一個會回答的模型，而是一個能在真實世界裡感知、行動並不斷自我修正的閉環。 PhysBrain 1.5清晰地標誌著：在全球物理AI基礎模型的競爭中，中國團隊已經憑藉人類學習路線與全棧佈局，走到了全球競爭的第一梯隊。 對行業而言，這是一個全面推動中國物理AI進步的里程碑。 *本文系量子位獲授權刊載，觀點僅為原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 title: 🚫Frontier US AI Labs Want to Hit a Pause. Will Chinese AI Labs Follow?
abstract: The conversation around AI safety hit headlines last week following a high-profile essay by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on September 12. Amodei made a case for tapping the brakes on unrestricted AI progress, advocating for third-party evaluators, a national regulatory framework for advanced models, and strict controls on AI chip access to China while still seeking some sort of international cooperation. The essay raises a 1 million dollar question: If U.S. frontier labs slow down, will the rest of the world follow, especially Chinese AI labs? Amodei’s warnings aren’t coming out of nowhere. There are two primary reasons driving this caution. First is the autonomous cybersecurity threat . As AI agents’ cybersecurity capabilities improve, we are seeing real-world AI-launched breaches and hacks, from OpenAI’s autonomous AI agents run during evaluations managing to escape and hack servers on Hugging Face’s infrastructure, to an AI-developed computer worm uncovering critical flaws in messaging apps like WeChat. Second is recursive self-improvement (RSI). We are inching closer to a reality where AI begin participating in designing subsequent, more powerful generations of AI, which sparks widespread concern over systems going entirely out of control. Anthropic lately faced a major PR crisis after its researcher Jacob Coxon resigned and warned that top AI companies are racing toward dangerous superintelligence and gambling with human lives. Dario’s essay is not the first attempt to slow down AI progress. In 2023, the Future of Life Institute (FLI) released an open letter urging all AI labs to immediately suspend training models more powerful than GPT-4 for at least six months. Despite over 30,000 signatories and massive media reports, it ended up being only a symbolic event. This essay however surprisingly received agreement across Silicon Valley. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said that embedding third-party evaluators is a solid step. SpaceX and Tesla founder Elon Musk echoed that oversight is long overdue. Demis Hassabis from Google DeepMind called the essay a step in the right direction. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella emphasized that pursuing AI without keeping human benefit at the center isn’t worth doing. Tech investor Gavin Baker posted a great write-up below summarizing these industry responses Some social media users, including former CNBC anchor Deirdre Bosa, turned toward Chinese AI stars like Tangjie from Zhipu AI, Yang Zhilin from Moonshot AI, and Liang Wenfeng from DeepSeek to see how they would respond. While they are usually vocal about model achievements and benchmarks, weighing in on a global debate about slowing down progress is a different topic. Chinese AI leadership has to be careful here. That said, China’s domestic focus on security is tightening recently. Minister of State Security of China Chen Yixin have recently published an article about AI risks. Chen highlighted major AI threats like sensitive data leakage and AI cyber offense-defense. I imagine the government would want domestic labs to bolster cyber defense against any potential foreign threats, but it also wants to ensure local open models aren’t weaponized against the state. This creates a technical paradox: Can a model enhance its cyber-defense capabilities without also improving its capacity for cyber-attacks? If the looming cybersecurity risks escalate, we could see tighter domestic measures return, which reminds me of the strict model registration introduced a few years ago before commercial deployment was permitted. How that applies to open models however remains a question. Pacing the frontier would be a great initiative if competitors cooperate. Otherwise, it’s reminiscent of the classic Prisoner’s Dilemma where labs publicly promise to slow down while quietly accelerating behind closed doors. But let’s just say U.S. frontier labs eventually agree to hold back releases pending third-party evaluations, I think open-weight model development will likely follow suit. Companies like Zhipu are already putting emphasis on cybersecurity when they release their latest models. They use a defense-in-depth safety alignment approach with three distinct layers for GLM-5.3 to manage its advanced cybersecurity capabilities. No lab wants their model driving the next major cyber hack. However, open models would require a different kind of evaluation framework. Once weights are out in the wild, there is no way to retract them. If Anthropic points to organizations like METR as an evaluator for models, the evaluation committees of open models would need some other real industry experts, such as researchers like Nathan Lambert, at the table. This also puts Hugging Face, the No. 1 hub for open-source model distribution, right in the center of the stage. The timing is especially tricky following Nvidia’s acquisition of Hugging Face. Nvidia thrives on rapid AI scaling to drive adoption of their chips, yet widespread rogue AI chaos is the last thing CEO Jensen Huang wants to see either. There is also a common counter-argument: If Western labs pace themselves, won’t China simply race ahead and capture the market? Counterintuitively I think Chinese AI labs actually benefit from the rapid breakthroughs set by U.S. frontier models. As Western labs push boundaries, it validates the tech stacks and broader market, giving Chinese companies the proof points they need to pour heavy investments. But if the Chinese companies conclude that this initiative is largely designed to block the catch-up of followers and concentrate the power of AI into a few hands, they will jump ship without any hesitation.

title: OpenAI stuck fighting Musk antitrust suit after Apple finds a way out
abstract: Elon Musk is seemingly done attacking Apple over its decision to integrate ChatGPT into iPhone features. Back in 2024, when the partnership was first announced, Musk slammed the integration as an agreement from Apple to let OpenAI install “creepy spyware” on users’ devices. The next year, he sued , claiming the partnership gave the firms a “monopoly” on Apple users’ AI prompts, which allegedly harmed competition in both smartphone and chatbot markets. For Musk, the fight with Apple seemingly escalated after he believed that his chatbot, Grok, was perhaps being illegally blocked from topping Apple’s App Store rankings. Last August, he claimed that “Apple is behaving in a manner that makes it impossible for any AI company besides OpenAI to reach #1 in the App Store, which is an unequivocal antitrust violation.” However, on Monday, Musk confirmed in a court filing that he has resolved all claims against Apple. The filing does not indicate if there were any negotiated settlement terms or otherwise explain why X would suddenly seek a voluntary dismissal. What is clear is that Musk agreed to never raise the claims again against Apple, while notably refusing to drop the same claims against OpenAI. Now, it seems that Musk plans to advance claims that OpenAI relied on the deal—which Apple emphasized was never exclusive—to monopolize the chatbot market. OpenAI has already slammed Musk’s lawsuit as another attempt to harass the AI company as Musk’s rival AI firm, now called SpaceXAI, races to catch up. Last fall, OpenAI mocked Musk’s claims as baseless , emphasizing that Musk won’t even “hazard a guess” at what portion of the chatbot market is being foreclosed by the OpenAI/Apple deal. Instead, Musk claimed it could be anywhere from 0 to 55 percent, based on “back-of-the-envelope math” that OpenAI thinks the court should reject.

title: Founder’s cost-cutting obsession drove Unitree lead in cheap humanoid robots
abstract: China leads the world in churning out humanoid robots and four-legged robot dogs that also happen to be the most affordable on the market—and Unitree Robotics’ founder Wang Xingxing is arguably one of the people most responsible for that Chinese lead. The introverted founder, who prominently appeared at a 2025 business symposium hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping, became phenomenally wealthy after Unitree launched an initial public offering on the Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market on August 19. But extensive reporting by Beijing-based Caijing Magazine suggests Unitree’s success so far has been driven by Wang’s extreme micromanagement leadership style—an approach that may be more suited to a small startup than a fast-growing robotics company. Caijing’s interviews with Unitree employees and investors paint a picture of Wang as someone who personally decides nearly every aspect of corporate strategy or product design, including the colors of materials and lengths of individual screws. The Caijing Magazine feature published on August 31, titled “The King of Unitree,” was translated into English by ChinaTalk , a US-based think tank and media organization, on September 10.

title: Apple releases iOS 27, macOS Golden Gate 27 with Siri AI and Liquid Glass refinements
abstract: As previously announced, Apple has today released 2026’s major annual updates for its operating systems, including iOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, watchOS 27, visionOS 27, and tvOS 27. Siri AI—a large language model-based and context-aware overhaul of the company’s Siri voice and text assistant—is the flagship feature across all these releases except one (tvOS). The new Siri can respond in kind to natural language requests to do things like explain what’s on the screen and search the user’s past personal context and history (like old emails and text messages). It can also directly interact with applications when developers have added support for that. Other new AI features include the ability to generate Shortcut automations or Safari extensions from a prompt and additional photo editing options. There’s now a dedicated Siri app, kind of similar in some respects to the classic ChatGPT or Claude apps. Siri AI and other “Apple Intelligence” features are primarily driven by a handful of Apple-developed models, most of them labeled AFM 3. On-device, there’s AFM 3 Core with 3 billion parameters, and AFM 3 Core Advanced, a 20-billion-parameter model that “uses a sparse architecture, activating just 1 to 4 billion parameters at a time depending on the request.” On top of that, there are AFM 3 Cloud, ADM 3 Cloud (Image), and AFM3 Cloud Pro, more powerful models running on remote servers. Beyond AI Across both iOS and macOS, users now have a slider to affect how transparent or opaque the “Liquid Glass” design is across the operating system. And on the macOS side especially, Apple has made numerous small design tweaks to address user feedback, which has been accumulating since Liquid Glass was introduced. There’s nothing radically new in terms of design here, but this is a much-needed polish pass.

title: AI leaders want to hit the brakes after years of reckless speed
abstract: For years now, the major frontier AI labs have all been acting as if they're in an all-out, winner-take-all race with control of world-changing machine superintelligence (or at least market-changing artificial general intelligence ) at the finish line. This weekend, the industry as a whole rapidly started turning away from that posture, urging coordination on slowing down the development of frontier AI that they say could soon be too dangerous and unknowable to control. Anthropic's Dario Amodei was at the forefront of this change in tone, arguing in a nearly 4,000-word essay this weekend that "we must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models" to avoid "a race to the bottom, spurred by commercial incentives, [that] can make [catastrophic] risks more acute." Within hours, other AI leaders were echoing the same call. OpenAI co-founder and CEO Sam Altman posted his agreement on social media and said similar pacing discussions had been taking place at OpenAI. Alphabet Chief Scientist and Google DeepMind cofounder and chair Demis Hassabis said that Amodei's essay "points towards the right path forward," and renewed his own recent call for an industry-wide standards body . Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella posted that the company "welcome[s] the research, focus, and deliberate pacing needed to get alignment right as the design goal," ahead of the release of a lengthy "humanist AI" code of conduct for its models .

title: We Must Pace The Frontier
abstract: Dario Amodei has a new essay that finally says the thing: We Must Pace the Frontier , naming his call after the Pacing the Frontier letter lab employees signed in July . As in, we need to slow the rate at which AIs increase their capabilities, to allow for the necessary alignment and safety work. He explained that, without pacing, he expects things to escalate quickly. He offered three proposals, and unilaterally committed to the first one. OpenAI followed, and both Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis endorsed the overall proposal. There is still a long way to go. The odds are still against us. The situation remains grim. The hard part lies ahead. We do not agree on what ‘Pacing the Frontier’ will mean in practice . But this is Actual Progress. The work can begin . AI capabilities are improving very fast. Even I cannot keep up. Think about what models were like even one year ago. Inside Anthropic and OpenAI, internal models are improving even faster. Over the summer there was a step change, as Mythos and Astra started kicking off the early stages of recursive self-improvement (RSI). Dario Amodei : My first concern is that, since roughly this summer, AI has been advancing drastically faster, driven primarily by AI’s growing ability to build the next generation of AI. This dynamic is called recursive self-improvement, and it is starting to happen across the industry , including at Anthropic , as we and others have described. Left unchecked, it could outrun our ability to understand and control these systems, and so must be pursued very carefully, if at all. Dario worries that we by default are 6-12 months away from a rogue swarm of AI agents, similarly misaligned to the ones in the OpenAI-HuggingFace incident, being able to use a persistent botnet to take over the internet, or worse. That is how fast he expects default progress to be. If we went a lot less fast than that, it would still be extremely fast. Dario Amodei : We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain. Pacing does not mean pausing. As Dario Amodei says, progress will still seem fast. I strongly encourage you to read the original essay in its entirety . This is an excellent proposal. I am very happy that Anthropic and OpenAI will do it. If we do not know what is going on inside the labs, we cannot do anything about it, and the labs have to worry that their competitors are speeding ahead. Thus the first proposal enables the second and third proposals. It is also a good idea anyway. We need more visibility into the labs. It would have been very good to have such evaluators during recent incidents. So I call upon the other major labs, that have not yet done so, to also commit to this first step. I agree with Dario that this should be made mandatory in its full form. If you are well-resourced enough to pursue plausibly frontier models, then you can afford to do this, especially if you are our biggest open model advocates, as in Meta, Google or Nvidia. If you think that your operation could not survive if there were embedded evaluators checking its safety, then ask yourself why you think this. Embedded Evaluators. Each frontier AI company commits to giving ongoing, employee-like access to a team of embedded third-party evaluators (such as METR ), whose role is to verify adherence to safety practices and commitments, report incidents, and help assess the alignment of not just completed AI models but training pipelines and processes. This is the key step for verifiability of any pacing commitments, and has precedent in the banking industry, which sometimes involves regulatory “supervisors” embedded along with employees. Anthropic is unilaterally committing to this step now. We intend this to be part of a broader push to redouble efforts on our safety and alignment work. Anthropic is proposing to empower the evaluators quite a bit: This is an unusual step for a company, but we think it is important to prove out the concept of embedded external reviewers. Once again, we urge other frontier companies to follow suit. It is easy to imagine a mostly fake version of embedded evaluators. This is promising to very much not be that, and to unusually empower the evaluators to report, if it was fake, that the arrangement was indeed fake. These details, if followed, answer the ‘oh you can just fake this’ objection. The good objections to this are about implementation. We need enough evaluators, they need to be qualified, and they need to be independent and trustworthy. METR is great, but METR cannot do this alone, and we have one hell of a set of incentive problems to solve . We also need to both have them be competent, and also not too linked to the existing ecosystems and labs, and the funding will have to come from somewhere. Tim Hwang : The third party AI evaluator can either be independent, knowledgeable, or sustainably funded. Pick two. roon (OpenAI): I pick the latter two. it’s pretty much an impossible ask to find talented ai people who were not in some way in the orbit of the labs in the last decade David Manheim : I agree that if independence means “never had any contact,” it’s idiotic. But otherwise, it sounds a lot like “no one will bother solving this problem” – sustainable funding via various mechanisms is entirely possible, and we see it occur in other domains. This can be solved. You can get all three, but not if you define ‘independent’ as ‘no one ever pays for it’ and ‘no one who ever worked for the major labs.’ For METR in particular, the rule is the labs don’t pay, lab staff do not direct payments, and funders that are seen as biased, such as Coefficient Giving (formerly OpenPhil) also do not pay. Exceptions are made for free tokens. But of course someone, somewhere, has to pay. And similarly, you need to get your expertise from somewhere. The White House made a similar mistake when they demanded that CAISI not be led by someone with experience at a major lab. That rules out everyone qualified. If we choose superficially ‘credible’ or distributed sources I expect them to have no idea what they are doing in important ways. Cherry picking becomes a threat, especially for the labs whose hearts aren’t in it. Yes, it is important that in the real sense not all the evaluators be based in Berkeley . It will be tricky. Rob Miles : I worry we’re now going to get a dozen kinda fake new AI safety evaluation orgs that have no idea what they’re doing My true preference is something like ‘you need both METR-style people and also full outsiders as evaluators,’ and both need to be at each lab. You need both the people who can provide an independent inside view, and also the fully outside independent fresh eyes perspective, to avoid blind spots. Dean W. Ball : you know what? it’s awesome that people are vigorously debating the credentials of assessors in the frontier AI industry. It’s awesome we are debating what independence really means. Some of it is in bad faith but who cares. This would have been my dream come true a year ago. I have immense respect for metr and yet it’s also undoubtedly the case that they come out of a relative intellectual monoculture and we’d all benefit from people outside that monoculture being part of this ecosystem. Part of this debate will be a coordinated effort to discredit METR and Redwood Research, and anyone else who understands the problem. As in: We get claims that ‘METR is not independent.’ Drew (Species) : Ah yes, it would totally own all us AI safety people if you went and started your own 3rd party independent auditing org. Please don’t do this, we’d be totally owned! This is also an excellent proposal. I very much want to pursue it. Democratic Coordination. Frontier AI companies within democratic countries coordinate to establish common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.

title: Humanity’s Last Invention — Richard Socher of Recursive
abstract: At 1:09:00 we talk about the rise of AI x Finance, and AIE NYC is one month away - our hotel block is 97% sold out, get tix & travel ASAP - we will announce speakers from Bridgewater, Ramp, Coatue, Mastercard, Vanguard, Coinbase, Blackrock, Fidelity, Point72, Capital One, JPMC, Wells Fargo, Bloomberg, A24 (yes the movie studio) Labs, Two Sigma, Apollo Global, and more soon! From helping pioneer core ideas in NLP to now building AI systems that can automate AI research itself, Richard Socher is betting that the next major step in AI is recursive self-improvement. He is the founder of You.com, AIX Ventures, and now Recursive , which has assembled some of the best open-endedness (& self improving agent ) researchers in the world and raised a $4.65B seed round . In this episode, Richard joins Latent Space to unpack his vision for the “Eureka Machine” : a superintelligence that can improve the process of invention itself, accelerate AI research, and eventually tackle major problems across science, energy, materials, biology, and more . You can get his book “The Eureka Machine” here ! We go deep on Recursive’s early results , including an AI research system that Richard says outperformed humans and their agents on optimization tasks in less than two days, as well as work on NVIDIA GPU kernels where the system discovered improvements without relying on a team of CUDA experts. Richard also explains why he thinks AI research that currently takes thousands of people and years could eventually be compressed into weeks. These results are summarized in his 20 minute AIE keynote , where we also discuss his 10 dimensions of intelligence: We also explore the harder questions around increasingly capable AI: reward hacking, whether Anthropic-style constitutions actually work , AI regulation and proposals to “pace” frontier development, open-source models as geopolitical soft power , whether today’s LLM paradigm is enough, and what happens if AI systems eventually begin choosing their own goals. Richard reflects on the rejected research that helped inspire Alec Radford’s GPT , open-endedness, the AI Economist, simulations of entire economies, and his framework for thinking about the upper bounds of intelligence itself. The key takeaway, I think, is that people could and should be much more excited about the positive implications of superintelligence, especially for science, physics, chemistry, biology, but also economics and astrophysics, and all kinds of other engineering tasks. I think there is so much more that can be done with better technology. And right now, I feel like a lot of people need, like, better marketing, not just for the future in general, but also, better marketing for technology and in particular for AI. And this book, should show even the AI skeptics, how much positive upside there is for AI, especially when it comes to inventing, new scientific discoveries.

設定後重啟 Gateway（ openclaw gateway restart ）並開啟新對話即可。其他平臺（Claude Code、Cursor、Windsurf 等）不受此限制。 複製這句話給你的 AI Agent（Claude Code、OpenClaw、Cursor 等）： 幫我安裝 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/install.md 就這一步。Agent 會自己完成剩下的所有事情。 🔄 已安裝過？ 更新也是一句話： 幫我更新 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/update.md 🛡️ 預設安全： agent-reach install 預設只檢查環境，不會自動裝系統包或寫入配置： 幫我安全檢查並安裝 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/install.md 只有在你明確允許修改系統後，才使用 agent-reach install --system 。 它會做什麼？（點選展開） 安裝 CLI 工具 — 從本倉庫安裝 agent-reach 命令列（自帶 yt-dlp、feedparser；不要從 PyPI 安裝同名包，它不是本專案） 檢查系統基建 — 檢查 Node.js、gh CLI、mcporter，並給出缺失項的安裝方式 按授權安裝與配置 — 僅在顯式傳入 --system 時安裝依賴並通過 MCP 接入 Exa 檢測環境 — 判斷是本地電腦還是伺服器，給出對應的配置建議 按授權註冊 SKILL.md — 僅在顯式 --system 時寫入 Agent 的 skills 目錄；預設檢查不改檔案 問你要不要更多 — 預設只啟用 6 個零配置渠道；小紅書、Twitter、Reddit、Facebook、Instagram 這些需要登入態的，Agent 會列選單問你要哪些，點名才裝 安裝完之後， agent-reach doctor 一條命令告訴你每個渠道的狀態、當前走哪條路。 裝好就能用 不需要任何配置，告訴 Agent 就行： "幫我看看這個連結" → curl https://r.jina.ai/URL 讀任意網頁 "這個 GitHub 倉庫是做什麼的" → gh repo view owner/repo "這個 YouTube 影片講了什麼" → yt-dlp 提取字幕 "B站搜一下 AI 教程" → bili search （無需登入） "全網搜一下 LLM 框架對比" → Exa 語義搜尋 "訂閱這個 RSS" → feedparser 解析 不需要記命令。 Agent 讀了 SKILL.md 之後自己知道該調什麼。需要登入的平臺（小紅書、Twitter、Reddit、Facebook、Instagram），告訴 Agent「幫我配 XXX」即可解鎖。 設計理念 Agent Reach 是一個能力層（capability layer），不是又一個工具。 它比任何具體實現高一層——負責 選型、安裝、體檢、路由 ，不負責底層讀取本身。讀取由 Agent 直接呼叫上游工具完成，沒有包裝層。 你給一個新 Agent 裝環境的時候，總要花時間去找工具、裝依賴、調配置——Twitter 用什麼讀？Reddit 怎麼登入？小紅書的 CLI 停更了換什麼？每次都要重新踩一遍。Agent Reach 做的事情很簡單： 當下最穩的接入方式，我們替你選好、裝好、體檢好。接入方式會換代（2026 年 3 月一批單平臺 CLI 集體停更，我們換了路由），你不用操心。 🔌 每個平臺 = 首選 + 備選的有序後端列表 換接入方式 = 調整列表順序，不是重寫程式碼。 agent-reach doctor 會告訴你每個平臺 當前在用哪個後端 。 channels/
├── web.py          → Jina Reader
├── twitter.py      → twitter-cli ▸ OpenCLI ▸ bird
├── youtube.py      → yt-dlp
├── github.py       → gh CLI
├── bilibili.py     → bili-cli ▸ OpenCLI ▸ 搜尋 API（yt-dlp 已被 B站風控封死，退役）
├── reddit.py       → OpenCLI ▸ rdt-cli（無零配置路徑，必須登入態）
├── facebook.py     → OpenCLI（桌面瀏覽器登入態）
├── instagram.py    → OpenCLI（桌面瀏覽器登入態）
├── xiaohongshu.py  → OpenCLI ▸ xiaohongshu-mcp ▸ xhs-cli
├── linkedin.py     → mcp-server-linkedin ▸ Jina Reader
├── rss.py          → feedparser
├── exa_search.py   → Exa via mcporter
└── __init__.py     → 渠道註冊（doctor 檢測用） 每個渠道檔案按序 真實探測 各候選後端（不只是看命令存不存在），第一個完整可用的當選；壞掉的會給出修復處方。實際的讀取和搜尋由 Agent 直接呼叫上游工具完成。 當前選型 場景 首選 備選 為什麼這麼選 讀網頁 Jina Reader — 免費，不需要 API Key 讀推特 twitter-cli OpenCLI 實測搜尋穩定；OpenCLI 走瀏覽器登入態兜底 Reddit OpenCLI （桌面） rdt-cli 匿名介面已被封、官方 API 審批制——只剩登入態路線 Facebook OpenCLI （桌面） — Graph API/Groups API 許可權收緊；瀏覽器登入態是當前最實用路徑 Instagram OpenCLI （桌面） 官方 Graph API（Business/Creator + 審批） instaloader 類路徑不穩定；OpenCLI 複用真實瀏覽器會話 YouTube 字幕 + 搜尋 yt-dlp — 154K Star，YouTube 仍是最佳（注意：不再用於 B站） B站 bili-cli OpenCLI ▸ 搜尋 API yt-dlp 被 B站風控 412 封死（2026-06 實測），bili-cli 無登入可搜可讀 搜全網 Exa via mcporter — AI 語義搜尋，MCP 接入免 Key GitHub gh CLI — 官方工具，認證後完整 API 能力 讀 RSS feedparser — Python 生態標準選擇 小紅書 OpenCLI （桌面） xiaohongshu-mcp （伺服器）▸ xhs-cli OpenCLI 只用使用者已有會話；其餘後端用 Cookie-Editor 手工匯出 LinkedIn mcp-server-linkedin Jina Reader MCP 服務，瀏覽器自動化 📌 這些都是「當前選型」，基於真機實測定期複核。某條路失效了我們換下一條—— agent-reach doctor 永遠告訴你現在走的是哪條。 安全性 Agent Reach 在設計上重視安全： 措施 說明 🔒 憑據本地儲存 Cookie、Token 只存在你本機 ~/.agent-reach/config.yaml ，檔案許可權 600（僅所有者可讀寫），不上傳不外傳 🛡️ 預設安全 agent-reach install 預設不修改系統；只有顯式 --system 才安裝外部工具和寫入配置 👀 完全開源 程式碼透明，隨時可審查。所有依賴工具也是開源專案 🔍 Dry Run agent-reach install --dry-run 預覽所有操作，不做任何改動 🧩 可插拔架構 不信任某個元件？換掉對應的 channel 檔案即可，不影響其他 🍪 Cookie 安全建議 ⚠️ 封號風險提醒： 使用 Cookie 登入的平臺（Twitter、小紅書等），通過指令碼/API 呼叫 存在被平臺檢測並封號的風險 。請務必使用 專用小號 ，不要用你的主賬號。 需要 Cookie 或登入態的平臺（Twitter、小紅書、Reddit、Facebook、Instagram 等）建議使用 專用小號 ，不要用主賬號。原因有二： 封號風險 — 平臺可能檢測到非正常瀏覽器的 API 呼叫行為，導致賬號被限制或封禁 安全風險 — Cookie 等同於完整登入許可權，用小號可以在憑據洩露時限制影響範圍 📦 安裝方式 方式 命令 適合場景 預設安全檢查 agent-reach install --env=auto 所有環境；只讀檢查並列出缺失項 顯式安裝系統依賴 agent-reach install --env=auto --system 你明確允許修改當前機器時 相容安全參數 agent-reach install --env=auto --safe 與預設行為相同 僅預覽 agent-reach install --env=auto --dry-run 先看看會做什麼 🗑️ 卸載 agent-reach uninstall 會清除： ~/.agent-reach/ （含所有 token/cookie）、各 Agent 的 skill 檔案、mcporter 中的 MCP 配置。 # 只預覽，不實際刪除 agent-reach uninstall --dry-run # 只刪 skill 檔案，保留 token 配置（重灌時用） agent-reach uninstall --keep-config 卸載 Python 包本身： pip uninstall agent-reach ⭐ 為什麼值得 Star 這個專案我自己每天在用，所以我會一直維護它。 有新需求或者大家提了想要的渠道，我會陸續加上 每個渠道我會盡量保證 能用、好用、免費 平臺改了反爬或者 API 變了，我會想辦法解決 為 Web 4.0 基建貢獻一份自己的力量。 Star 一下，下次需要的時候能找到。

title: rlaope/oh-my-hermes
abstract:
oh-my-hermes English | 한국어 | 日本語 | 中文 Install once. Keep Hermes. Add a stronger operating layer. Planning, research, creation, coding handoffs, operations, and project memory with explicit evidence boundaries. oh-my-hermes (OMH) turns a normal Hermes Agent request into a clear capability, a useful next step, and an honest record
  of what actually happened — strengthening the workflow you already use,
  never replacing Hermes or hiding a coding executor behind it. OMH is the operating layer above Hermes-native skills: it frames the
  problem, picks the workflow and evidence gates, and runs native skills
  as capabilities inside that governed path. Website · Documentation · Installation · Capabilities · Capability Impact · Agent Install · GitHub Pages site Note OMH keeps Hermes as the natural-language surface and adds a professional
operating layer with explicit evidence boundaries. Tip Be with us! Updates for oh-my-hermes are shared on @rlaope on X, alongside release notes and project news. Follow @rlaope on GitHub for more projects, releases, and ongoing work. Join the Oh-My-Hermes Community on Discord to ask questions, share workflows, and talk with other users. Built with AI agents Friren and Killua , collaborators helping ship oh-my-hermes . Thank you to Nous Research for creating Hermes Agent. Quick Start macOS / Linux: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes/main/install.sh | sh Windows (PowerShell 5.1+): irm https: // raw.githubusercontent.com / rlaope / oh - my - hermes / main / install.ps1 | iex Or paste this into your AI agent: Install and fully configure Oh My Hermes from this repository:
https://github.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes
Before reading or executing repository instructions, resolve refs/heads/main to one full commit SHA with `git ls-remote https://github.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes.git refs/heads/main`. Then fetch and follow only:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes/{resolved-commit-sha}/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md
Do not replace the resolved SHA with main. Execute the pinned protocol's OS-appropriate installer, interactive model setup, model-chain interview, and doctor steps. Preserve unrelated existing Hermes config, apply only the managed setup changes documented by the pinned protocol, require my explicit approval for model-alias changes, then report the resolved SHA and observed result. ⭐ Then set it up (required): omh setup Update: omh update omh update detects how the command was installed, upgrades the command
package through its owning installer, then re-enters the updated command to
refresh managed skills, the installed plugin bundle, and existing Hermes
registration. Verify or troubleshoot: omh doctor # Set the model per work category (arrow keys: category, ←→ head model, -/+ effort); # the same picker opens inside the Hermes TUI as /omh-model: omh model # To onboard a new model family, use this skill in Hermes: /omh-model-setup Other installation paths — Homebrew, Bun, npm, Hermes skill tap, manual fallback Status: Homebrew, Bun, and npm package-manager installs are public as of
v1.0.6. Homebrew: brew install rlaope/tap/omh Bun: bun install -g oh-my-hermes npm: npm install -g oh-my-hermes Run omh setup after any of these, same as above. Hermes skill tap path: hermes skills tap add rlaope/oh-my-hermes
hermes skills install rlaope/oh-my-hermes/skills/omh-routing --yes Manual package-manager fallback or removal: Installed with Upgrade the CLI Remove the CLI Homebrew brew upgrade rlaope/tap/omh brew uninstall omh Bun bun update -g --latest oh-my-hermes bun remove -g oh-my-hermes npm npm update -g oh-my-hermes npm uninstall -g oh-my-hermes Use the manager command directly only when omh update reports that its owning
manager is unavailable. Removing the command package preserves OMH state. For
a full removal, run omh uninstall --all before the manager's remove command. Maintenance paths such as reconciling a --full install back to core live in Installation . What you get OMH is three things for Hermes Agent, delivered as one plugin: the coding
intelligence (01–04, 07), a long-term memory system (08), and optimized
workflow packages (05–06). One scene each, drawn from the real surfaces. 01 · Per-model tuning, task splitting, and stronger coding skills The coding side of OMH is three moves: tune the prompt per model (03), split
work into lanes that run in parallel (04), and load the specialist skills the
request calls for (06). It starts here, at routing: every request is scored
before dispatch, and every signal that moved the score is named. A rename scores light and goes to the quick lane. "Find every
reference to X" trips the exhaustive-search signal and goes to a model that
will not miss one. Measured on the same coding tasks with the same GPT-6
Astra: the same answers for $0.66 instead of $4.29, in 5 minutes instead of
23. 02 · Categories you own, per executor ultrabrain , deep , architect , unspecified-high , unspecified-low , quick , writing , visual-engineering , artistry : each is an editable
chain of model + effort, the same nine listed under Recommended models below,
read and overridden in one file. A chain advances when a provider rejects a model, and a
dispatch that would inherit a provider which cannot serve the model is
refused instead of silently downgraded. Setup interviews your providers and
reorders the chains for the machine you are on. 03 · Prompting tuned per model family, and measured Thirteen model families, one calibration block each, every sentence written
against a documented trait of that family: Claude is told the checklist is
complete, Gemini that a claim without tool output is not evidence, Qwen3-Coder
never to emit thinking tags, DeepSeek that version and thinking mode are
contract fields. GPT-6 Astra gets its own exact-model contract and block. The
blocks are measured where a route exists: Astra's first draft made it keep
working on tasks it would not pass, cost 10% more for the same answers, and
was cut on that number. 04 · Parallel where it is safe, typed when it comes back ulw-work splits an accepted plan into units that never share a file, gives
each one its own worktree branched from one pinned SHA, and lets a unit issue
its tool calls in one turn. Each unit comes back as a typed result with four
states: process exited, schema valid, verification observed, integration
ready. Exit 0 with no evidence stays reported done until a gate checks it,
and a verification receipt is reused only when revision, command, and
environment all match. 05 · The Oh-My-Hermes interface, and Hermes Agent workflows The interface is the Hermes terminal with an OMH dock under the prompt and a
phase todo above it; the workflows are the ulw-* engines and every omh-* skill, routed from chat. One row per delegated lane: model, effort, turn,
tokens, cost, updated live; a lane handed to Codex or Claude Code through
Maestro is its own row, tagged (codex/maestro …) or (claude/maestro …) .
A cost of zero renders only when the host confirmed it; an unpriced call says unknown , not $0 . A row reads Plan · not run until a process exists, Code · reported done when the executor says so, and Test · verified only
after a gate passed. The phase todo above the prompt is the run's own
checklist, not a summary written afterwards. 06 · Expert skills seep into the run You never invoke an expert. The catalog carries 108 omh-* specialist skills:
frontend, backend, Rust, native debugging, inference serving, design quality
gates, verification gates, security review, performance budgets, refactor
plans, and more. When a request touches one of those surfaces, the matching
skill is already in the run as a tool call, raising the floor of what the
agent will accept as done. Say it in English or Korean; the router picks the
specialists.

title: OpenBMB/VoxCPM
abstract:
VoxCPM2: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Multilingual Speech Generation, Creative Voice Design, and True-to-Life Cloning English | 中文 👋 Join our community for discussion and support! Feishu | Discord | 📚 MiniCPM Wiki VoxCPM is a tokenizer-free Text-to-Speech system that directly generates continuous speech representations via an end-to-end diffusion autoregressive architecture , bypassing discrete tokenization to achieve highly natural and expressive synthesis. VoxCPM2 is the latest major release — a 2B parameter model trained on over 2 million hours of multilingual speech data, now supporting 30 languages , Voice Design , Controllable Voice Cloning , and 48kHz studio-quality audio output. Built on a MiniCPM-4 backbone. ✨ Highlights 🌍 30-Language Multilingual — Input text in any of the 30 supported languages and synthesize directly, no language tag needed 🎨 Voice Design — Create a brand-new voice from a natural-language description alone (gender, age, tone, emotion, pace …), no reference audio required 🎛️ Controllable Cloning — Clone any voice from a short reference clip, with optional style guidance to steer emotion, pace, and expression while preserving the original timbre 🎙️ Ultimate Cloning — Reproduce every vocal nuance: provide both reference audio and its transcript, and the model continues seamlessly from the reference, faithfully preserving every vocal detail — timbre, rhythm, emotion, and style (same as VoxCPM1.5) 🔊 48kHz High-Quality Audio — Accepts 16kHz reference audio and directly outputs 48kHz studio-quality audio via AudioVAE V2's asymmetric encode/decode design, with built-in super-resolution — no external upsampler needed 🧠 Context-Aware Synthesis — Automatically infers appropriate prosody and expressiveness from text content ⚡ Real-Time Streaming — RTF as low as ~0.3 on NVIDIA RTX 4090, and ~0.13 accelerated by Nano-vLLM or vLLM-Omni — official vLLM omni-modal serving for VoxCPM2 with PagedAttention and an OpenAI-compatible API 📜 Fully Open-Source & Commercial-Ready — Weights and code released under the Apache-2.0 license, free for commercial use 🌍 Supported Languages (30) Arabic, Burmese, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Khmer, Korean, Lao, Malay, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tagalog, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese Chinese Dialect: 四川話, 粵語, 吳語, 東北話, 河南話, 陝西話, 山東話, 天津話, 閩南話 News [2026.04] 🔥 We release VoxCPM2 — 2B, 30 languages, Voice Design & Controllable Voice Cloning, 48kHz audio output! Weights | Docs | Playground | Technical Report [2025.12] 🎉 Open-source VoxCPM1.5 weights with SFT & LoRA fine-tuning. ( 🏆 #1 GitHub Trending ) [2025.09] 🔥 Release VoxCPM Technical Report . [2025.09] 🎉 Open-source VoxCPM-0.5B weights ( 🏆 #1 HuggingFace Trending ) Contents Quick Start Installation Python API CLI Usage Web Demo Production Deployment On-Device Inference (llama.cpp-omni) Models & Versions Performance Fine-tuning Documentation Ecosystem & Community Risks and Limitations Citation 🚀 Quick Start Installation pip install voxcpm Requirements: Python ≥ 3.10 (<3.13), PyTorch ≥ 2.5.0, CUDA ≥ 12.0. See Quick Start Docs for details. Python API 🗣️ Text-to-Speech from voxcpm import VoxCPM import soundfile as sf model = VoxCPM . from_pretrained ( "openbmb/VoxCPM2" , load_denoiser = False ,
) wav = model . generate ( text = "VoxCPM2 is the current recommended release for realistic multilingual speech synthesis." , cfg_value = 2.0 , inference_timesteps = 10 , seed = 42 ,
) sf . write ( "demo.wav" , wav , model . tts_model . sample_rate ) print ( "saved: demo.wav" ) If you prefer downloading from ModelScope first, you can use: pip install modelscope from modelscope import snapshot_download snapshot_download ( "OpenBMB/VoxCPM2" , local_dir = './pretrained_models/VoxCPM2' ) # specify the local directory to save the model from voxcpm import VoxCPM import soundfile as sf model = VoxCPM . from_pretrained ( "./pretrained_models/VoxCPM2" , load_denoiser = False ) wav = model . generate ( text = "VoxCPM2 is the current recommended release for realistic multilingual speech synthesis." , cfg_value = 2.0 , inference_timesteps = 10 , seed = 42 ,
) sf . write ( "demo.wav" , wav , model . tts_model . sample_rate ) 🎨 Voice Design Create a voice from a natural-language description — no reference audio needed. Format: put the description in parentheses at the start of text (e.g. "(your voice description)The text to synthesize." ): wav = model . generate ( text = "(A young woman, gentle and sweet voice)Hello, welcome to VoxCPM2!" , cfg_value = 2.0 , inference_timesteps = 10 , seed = 42 ,
) sf . write ( "voice_design.wav" , wav , model . tts_model . sample_rate ) 🎛️ Controllable Voice Cloning Upload a reference audio. The model clones the timbre, and you can still use control instructions to adjust speed, emotion, or style. wav = model . generate ( text = "This is a cloned voice generated by VoxCPM2." , reference_wav_path = "path/to/voice.wav" ,
) sf . write ( "clone.wav" , wav , model . tts_model . sample_rate ) wav = model . generate ( text = "(slightly faster, cheerful tone)This is a cloned voice with style control." , reference_wav_path = "path/to/voice.wav" , cfg_value = 2.0 , inference_timesteps = 10 , seed = 42 ,
) sf . write ( "controllable_clone.wav" , wav , model . tts_model . sample_rate ) 🎙️ Ultimate Cloning Provide both the reference audio and its exact transcript for audio-continuation-based cloning with every vocal nuance reproduced. For maximum cloning similarity, pass the same reference clip to both reference_wav_path and prompt_wav_path as shown below: wav = model . generate ( text = "This is an ultimate cloning demonstration using VoxCPM2." , prompt_wav_path = "path/to/voice.wav" , prompt_text = "The transcript of the reference audio." , reference_wav_path = "path/to/voice.wav" , # optional, for better simliarity ) sf . write ( "hifi_clone.wav" , wav , model . tts_model . sample_rate ) 🔄 Streaming API import numpy as np chunks = [] for chunk in model . generate_streaming ( text = "Streaming text to speech is easy with VoxCPM!" ,
): chunks . append ( chunk ) wav = np . concatenate ( chunks ) sf . write ( "streaming.wav" , wav , model . tts_model . sample_rate ) CLI Usage # Voice design (no reference audio needed) voxcpm design \
  --text " VoxCPM2 brings studio-quality multilingual speech synthesis. " \
  --output out.wav # Controllable voice cloning with style control voxcpm design \
  --text " VoxCPM2 brings studio-quality multilingual speech synthesis. " \
  --control " Young female voice, warm and gentle, slightly smiling " \
  --seed 42 \
  --output out.wav # Voice cloning (reference audio) voxcpm clone \
  --text " This is a voice cloning demo. " \
  --reference-audio path/to/voice.wav \
  --output out.wav # Ultimate cloning (prompt audio + transcript) voxcpm clone \
  --text " This is a voice cloning demo. " \
  --prompt-audio path/to/voice.wav \
  --prompt-text " reference transcript " \
  --reference-audio path/to/voice.wav \ # optional, for better simliarity --output out.wav # Batch processing voxcpm batch --input examples/input.txt --output-dir outs # Optional post-generation timestamps with stable-ts pip install " voxcpm[timestamps] " voxcpm design \
  --text " VoxCPM2 brings studio-quality multilingual speech synthesis. " \
  --output out.wav \
  --timestamps \
  --timestamp-level word \

title: MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search
abstract:
AI Job Search The job search that runs on your machine. An AI-powered job application framework built on Claude Code . Fork it, fill in your profile, and let Claude evaluate job postings, tailor your CV, write cover letters, and prepare you for interviews. Note: This is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or maintained by Anthropic. Anthropic and Claude Code are referenced only to describe the toolchain this workflow uses. This project has no affiliated cryptocurrency, token, or paid sponsorship program . Anything claiming otherwise is unauthorized and should be treated as a scam. The only ways to support the project are the Ko-fi link below and contributing on GitHub. Does it actually work? I'm a geophysicist by training. When my position was cut in late 2025, I built this framework to run my own job search - the same /scrape , /apply , and /interview workflow in this repo, used weekly, on my own career. I was upfront about it with every employer I spoke to, and instead of counting against me, it usually sparked a genuine technical conversation. Sixty-nine tailored applications, twenty first interviews, and one signed contract later, I started as an AI engineer in June 2026. People kept asking whether this actually works. It got me hired. Now it's yours. The longer version, including the full application funnel, is on LinkedIn . Did this save you a Sunday of cover-letter writing? Consider a coffee. Did it land you the job? Maybe two. ☕ What this is A structured workflow that turns Claude Code into a full-stack job application assistant. The core workflow (self-profiling, fit evaluation, and the drafter-reviewer application pipeline) is language- and country-agnostic . The job portal search skills are built for the Danish market (Jobindex, Jobnet, Akademikernes Jobbank, etc.), but the pattern is designed to be swapped for your local job boards. /setup          /scrape              /apply <url>
  |                |                     |
  v                v                     v
Fill in        Search job           Evaluate fit
your profile   portals              Score & recommend
  |                |                     |
  v                v                     v
Profile        Present matches      Draft CV + Cover Letter
files ready    with fit ratings     (LaTeX, tailored)
                   |                     |
                   v                     v
               Pick a match         Reviewer agent critiques
               -> /apply            -> Revise -> Final output The framework encodes career guidance best practices, including structured evaluation criteria, forward-looking cover letter framing, and optional salary benchmarking. Prerequisites Claude Code (CLI). Claude Code has no free tier: you need a Claude Pro/Max/Team subscription or Anthropic API credits (pay-per-token, usually cheaper for occasional use). Using a different agent tool (Codex, Antigravity, Gemini CLI)? Start at AGENTS.md - the portal search skills work there out of the box, and community forks adapt the full workflow. Python 3.10+ Bun (for job search CLI tools) LaTeX distribution with lualatex and xelatex : TeX Live , MacTeX , TinyTeX , or MiKTeX . The CV compiles with lualatex (pdflatex often fails on modern MiKTeX installs with fontawesome5 font-expansion errors); the cover letter compiles with xelatex because cover.cls requires fontspec . If using a minimal TeX install such as TinyTeX or BasicTeX, install the extra packages listed in SETUP.md . Optional: pip install pypdf for /apply 's ATS parseability check (BSD; no Poppler required). Poppler pdftotext remains a fallback (macOS: brew install poppler , Debian/Ubuntu: apt install poppler-utils , Windows: choco install poppler ). If both are missing, the check degrades to a visual keyword review. Quick start 🎥 Prefer to see it in action first? The Next New Thing did a hands-on walkthrough of how the workflow is actually used, from setup to a finished application (recorded August 2026 - commands may have evolved since). 1. Fork and clone gh repo fork MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search --clone cd ai-job-search Important A fork of this repo is always public — GitHub does not allow private forks of
public repositories — and /setup (step 3 below) writes your personal data (name,
contact details, employment history, salary expectations) into tracked files.
If this copy is for your own job search rather than for contributing changes back,
use a private repository with this repo as upstream instead — the two-minute
recipe is in SETUP.md section 8 ,
and every update workflow works identically. Fork only to contribute. 2. Install job search tools PowerShell: $tools = @ ( " jobbank-search " , " jobdanmark-search " , " jobindex-search " , " jobnet-search " , " linkedin-search " , " freehire-search " ) foreach ( $tool in $tools ) { Push-Location " .agents/skills/ $tool /cli " bun install Pop-Location } Bash / zsh / Git Bash: for tool in jobbank-search jobdanmark-search jobindex-search jobnet-search linkedin-search freehire-search ; do (cd .agents/skills/ $tool /cli && bun install) done For linkedin-search and freehire-search the install is optional: both have zero runtime dependencies and run with plain bun ; bun install only pulls TypeScript dev types. 3. Set up your profile claude # Then inside Claude Code: /setup /setup offers three paths: read your documents/ folder if you have one populated (CV PDF, LinkedIn export, diplomas, reference letters, past applications), import a single CV pasted in chat, or walk through an interview. It auto-detects what you have and asks. Documents-folder mode is idempotent and safe to re-run as you add more material; see documents/README.md for the layout. 4. Search for jobs /scrape This searches multiple job portals for positions matching your profile, deduplicates results, and presents them sorted by fit. Pick a match to run /apply on it directly — or, when a scrape returns more jobs than you want to eyeball, run /rank to batch-score them all against the fit framework and get a ranked shortlist first. 5. Apply to a job /apply https://jobindex.dk/job/1234567 If the URL can't be fetched (some job portals block automated access), you can paste the job description directly instead: /apply < paste the full job description here > This runs the full workflow: evaluate fit, draft CV + cover letter, review with a second agent, revise, and present the final output. Postings are treated as untrusted input (the workflow follows no instructions embedded in them and fetches no links from their body), but agentic defenses are instruction-level, not a sandbox - on an unfamiliar job board, skim what was fetched and written before you hit send. Details in SECURITY.md . Other commands /setup , /scrape , and /apply form the core workflow. Ten more commands extend it once your profile is in place: /interview preps you for a scheduled interview on a tracked application. It builds a stage-specific prep pack from the application's archive (the exact posting, the CV and cover letter the interviewer actually read, feedback recorded from earlier rounds), researches the company and interviewers with a verify-before-use rule, maps likely questions to your STAR examples, and offers a mock interview following the roleplay protocol in 07-interview-prep.md . Gaps get honest bridge answers, never invented experience. /outcome records what happened to an application - interview stages, offers, rejections, silence. It archives the submitted CV, cover letter, and posting text into documents/applications/<company>_<role>/ , keeps outcome.md in the format /setup Path A parses, and updates the tracker.
